vedic_philosophy_astronomy.introduction: Astronomy in the Indian tradition is closely connected to timekeeping, ritual calendars, and observation of celestial cycles. In Sanātana Dharma, the study of the sky supports practical life (agriculture, seasons) as well as sacred life (tithis, nakshatras, festivals, and auspicious timings). This page is an overview of the astronomy-related knowledge streams often grouped under jyotisha and related disciplines, presented as a cultural and philosophical tradition of careful observation and structured calculation.

vedic_philosophy_astronomy.philosophical_explanation: A philosophical theme behind traditional astronomy is reverence for order (ṛta) and rhythm. The sky’s regularity becomes a teacher: patience, humility, and the ability to align human activity with larger cycles. In practice, this fosters discipline and attention—qualities also emphasized in spiritual life.

scripture_text.content: Astronomy and calendrical computation appear in many traditional sources, including Vedanga literature (especially jyotisha), later siddhanta texts, and temple almanacs (panchangam). Rather than quoting specific verses here, this site focuses on concepts: cycles, measurements, and how calendars are constructed and used.
